title: Confusion, purpura and anaemia — focused assessment, critical decision and communication

blocks.text: Confusion, purpura and anaemia — focused assessment, critical decision and communication
AMaC MRCP PACES23 | R5-226 | Station 2: Acute consultation | Skills A–G; appropriate clinical assessment | 20 minutes | AMaC educational mark grid, not official MRCP(UK) marks.

A 38-year-old has new bruises, confusion, severe fatigue and a markedly low platelet count. Take a focused history and explain your immediate plan. A nurse can provide observations or blood results on request.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: Hook: Suspected immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP). Trap: Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with thrombocytopenia and neuro features is a time-critical TTP presentation.

rows: “Before anything else, I need to check whether you are seriously unwell.”
“I have a few specific questions to help work out the cause.”
Assess consciousness, focal neurology, bleeding and cardiac symptoms. Check FBC, film for schistocytes, LDH, bilirubin, reticulocytes, renal function, clotting, troponin and haemolysis markers.
“I am concerned about a potentially serious condition.”
“I will explain the tests and what happens next.”

Call haematology immediately; take plasma for ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor before plasma if this does not delay treatment; start urgent therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids on strong suspicion. Consider caplacizumab and rituximab under a specialist protocol.

blocks.text: You are frightened and ask “Can I go home?” Give the opening complaint spontaneously; answer focused questions consistently with examiner findings. Ask one question about long-term consequences or family safety as appropriate.

THINK: Suspected immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP). SAY: acknowledge uncertainty. DO: Call haematology immediately; take plasma for ADAMTS13 activity and inhibitor before plasma if this does not delay treatment; start urgent therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids on strong suspicion. Consider caplacizumab and rituximab under a specialist protocol. NUMBERS: 20-minute PACES encounter. TRAP: Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with thrombocytopenia and neuro features is a time-critical TTP presentation. FINISH: Do not await ADAMTS13 to treat a high-probability case. Avoid prophylactic platelet transfusion unless life-threatening bleeding or exceptional specialist indication.
